newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MANCINI'S ABSENCE WEIGHS ON SAMPDORIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MANCINI'S ABSENCE WEIGHS ON SAMPDORIA.

text.p: The absence of experienced Roberto Mancini weighed heavily on Sampdoria's young shoulders on Sunday as the second-placed serie A side lost their seven-match unbeaten record to Roma and fell five points behind leaders Juventus.
Without the suspended Mancini and first-choice goalkeeper Fabrizio Ferron, Samp's youthful team were a pale shadow of the side that beat Milan 3-2 on their last outing.
Roma, using the counter-attack to lethal effect, went ahead in the 44th minute when Francesco Moriero fired home after a superb defence-splitting pass from Swede Jonas Thern.
After the break, Samp's title chances were further compromised when inexperienced Matteo Sereni, the 22-year-old replacement for Ferron, dropped a corner leaving Balbo with a simple tap-in.

Vincenzo Montella revived Sampdoria's hopes when he claimed his 13th goal of the season but they were condemned to a 2-1 defeat when Roma goalkeeper Giovanni Cervone saved former team mate Sinisa Mihajlovic's curling freekick in the last minute.
Alessandro Del Piero made sure that Juventus took maximum advantage of Samp's slip-up, with both goals in his side's 2-1 win over struggling Perugia.

Del Piero, left on the substitutes' bench for Italy's World Cup win over England last week, put Juve ahead in the 37th minute from the penalty spot before scoring a superlative second in the 45th -- a smooth turn and shot from just inside the area.
Victory leaves Juventus five points clear at the top with 40 points from 20 matches.
Bologna, Inter and Atalanta lie a distant third on 31 points although Parma will move ahead of this group if they win their derby on Sunday night with bottom-placed Reggiana.
Lazio's former manager Zdenek Zeman, replaced by Dino Zoff last month, was a surprise onlooker at the Olympic stadium for his old team's clash with Inter.
But for most of the match, Lazio's fans could have been forgiven for thinking Zeman was still on the bench.

True to the unpredictable performances of Zeman's sides, Lazio took the lead through Diego Fuser's first goal of the season in the 25th minute, and then, went behind as they conceded two goals in as many minutes.

Chilean striker Ivan Zamorano levelled the scores before French playmaker Youri Djorkaeff put Inter ahead. Giuseppe Signori, however, spared Lazio's blushes with his 100th goal in the club's colours in the 73rd minute.
Serie A's top scorer Filippo Inzaghi took his season's tally to 15 with two goals in Atalanta's 3-1 win over Vicenza -- the second, a thumping 25 metre drive into the roof of the net.
After the match, manager Emilio Mondonico dedicated the Bergamo side's 10th league match without defeat to the late Federico Pisani, the 22-year-old striker killed in a car crash last Wednesday.

After two defeats in their last three matches, Milan president Silvio Berlusconi had suggested his side needed a trip to Lourdes. Against Bologna, there were no miracles but they had their share of luck as Demetrio Albertini converted a 45th minute penalty for a foul on George Weah when the Liberian looked suspiciously offside.

Jesper Blomqvist sealed Milan's first victory in four matches with his first goal since joining the club from Gothenburg last November. But the Swede's celebrations were cut short with a red card four minutes later after a vicious foul on Igor Shalimov.
At Verona, Russian Andrea Kanchelskis made a disappointing debut for Fiorentina, who lost 2-1 at third-from-bottom Verona.
